candidate_relations.reason: Both Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) and Xanthoma disseminatum (XD) are non-Langerhans cell histiocytoses that are CD1a-negative and CD68-positive, and both can involve systemic manifestations including diabetes insipidus. However, ECD is a distinct entity primarily affecting adults with characteristic long-bone osteosclerosis, perirenal/retroperitoneal infiltration, and BRAF V600E mutations, whereas XD classically presents in young patients with mucocutaneous xanthomatous papules/nodules, normolipidemia, and diabetes insipidus without the skeletal and retroperitoneal involvement typical of ECD. The clinical presentation here—teenage onset, widespread reddish-brown papules starting at eyelid margins, central diabetes insipidus, growth retardation, hypothyroidism, and the described biopsy with foam cells and multinucleated giant cells—is far more consistent with XD. C001 asserts an incompatible specific entity rather than the benchmark diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Erdheim-Chester disease is a distinct non-Langerhans histiocytosis with overlapping features but different clinical profile and classification from Xanthoma disseminatum

case_quality_flags: Classic Xanthoma disseminatum presentation with periocular onset, normolipidemic xanthomas, and pituitary/hypothalamic involvement; CD1a/S-100 negativity with CD68 positivity appropriately excludes Langerhans cell histiocytosis
